name: China economy
value: Q3 GDP +4.5%; Oct activity data due 16 Nov
summary: China's Q3 growth was 4.5% and October prices rose, so no deflation; October activity data are due on 16 Nov
state: China's economy grew 4.5% a year in the third quarter, beating forecasts on strong exports, while property investment kept falling (CNBC, 19 Oct). October consumer prices rose 0.7% and producer prices 5.7%, ruling out deflation, though credit demand stayed weak. The statistics bureau's calendar schedules October industrial output and retail sales for 16 Nov; searches on 15 Nov found no new developer default wave or financial contagion.
for_you: Firms trading with China are most exposed to its slow property sector and weak household borrowing. No acute disruption to trade or finance is evident.
rubric_hit: Normal: Q3 growth 4.5%, near target; no deflation (CPI +0.7%) or financial contagion

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
